latin.647: Quod Adami peccatum nobis per imputationem convenit, vel, si ita mavis, nobis proxime & immediate imputatur, id ex quo sumus reipsa neque a nobis commissum est, neque nobis inhaeret. Res manifesta est de peccato actuali Adami: id enim vis nobis imputari, non autem inesse, aut a nobis natis committi.
latin.648: Nam quod per imputationem convenit, non convenit per realem inhaerentiam sive inexistientiam. Duo istiusmodi inter se pugnant. Cur enim aut faciam aut patiar quod alius loco meo vel fecit vel passus est?
latin.649: Atqui si peccatum actuale Adami nobis imputatur, profecto etiam imputatur eius peccatum habituale sive corruptio inhaerens. Nam quae ratio afferri potest pro imputatione peccati actualis Adami, quae eadem non militet pro imputatione peccati eiusdem habitualis, & quidem validius? Illud enim fuit actio praeteriens, hoc vitium permanens: illud iam pridem praeterierat cum anno aetatis 130. Adamus Sethum genuit, a quo nos ducimus originem; hoc vero tum aderat praesens & inhaerens penitus facultatibus Adami cum generationi operam daret.
latin.650: Illud vulgo dicitur esse personae, hoc naturae. Itaque aut aeque aut magis etiam conveniebat Adamo ut capiti nostro & origini, & nostram personam sustinenti, quam peccatum illud actuale, quod actio fuit singularis.
latin.651: Si ergo peccatum actuale Adami nobis imputatur, imputatur etiam nobis eius vitium sive peccatum habituale & insitum. Si imputatur, non est in nobis. Quod enim nobiscum Adamus communicavit imputatione, id non communicavit nobiscum reali existentia. Quod peccatum peccavimus in persona Adami, id non peccavimus realiter in nostris personis postea quam geniti sumus.
latin.652: Alioqui magis peccatores ex Adamo nasceremur quam fuit Adam. Nam ei non est imputatum nisi ipsius peccatum actuale & habituale; nobis idem utrumque, quemadmodum Adamo, imputaretur, & praeterea imputaretur idem specie peccatum habituale nobis actu insitum ac inhaerens: nam, velis nolis, corruptio innata peccatum est, nisi condonetur, imputandum ad mortem.

pass_a.647: Placeus states the target claim: Adam's sin 'ours by imputation' (or immediately imputed) is, as to us, neither our deed nor inherent in us. Garrigues wants Adam's actual sin imputed, not inesse or done by us once born.
pass_a.648: Imputation and real inherence fight: what comes one way does not come the other. Why should I do or suffer what another did or suffered in my place?
pass_a.649: If Adam's actual sin is imputed to us, Placeus says his habitual sin—inherent corruption—must be imputed too, and more strongly. The paradise act was a passing deed already gone when Adam at 130 begot Seth; the vice was present and deep in his powers when he generated.
pass_a.650: Common tag: the act is of the person, the vice of nature—so the vitium fits Adam as head/origin sustaining our person even more than the singular paradise act.
pass_a.651: So if Adam's actual sin is imputed, his implanted habitual vice is too; and if it is imputed, it is not in us. What Adam shared by imputation he did not share by real existence—the sin we 'sinned in Adam's person' we did not really sin in our own persons after birth.
pass_a.652: Tip reductio: otherwise we would be born more sinners than Adam was—only his actual and habitual imputed to him, but to us both of those plus a like habitual actually infused and inherent (innate corruption is sin to be imputed unto death unless forgiven). Tip before equity/Martyr.

647: That Adam's sin belongs to us by imputation—or, if you prefer, is proximately and immediately imputed to us—is, as far as we are concerned in the thing itself, neither committed by us nor inherent in us. The matter is plain about Adam's actual sin: for you want that imputed to us, not to be in us, or to be committed by us once born.
648: For what belongs by imputation does not belong by real inherence or inexistence. Those two fight each other. For why should I either do or suffer what another has done or suffered in my place?
649: And if Adam's actual sin is imputed to us, then certainly his habitual sin—or inherent corruption—is imputed too. For what reason can be offered for imputing Adam's actual sin that does not equally—and more strongly—serve for imputing his habitual sin? That was a passing act; this is a permanent vice. That had already long passed when, at age 130, Adam begot Seth, from whom we take our origin; but this was then present and thoroughly inherent in Adam's powers when he gave himself to generation.
650: That is commonly said to belong to the person; this, to the nature. So it suited Adam as our head and origin, and as sustaining our person, equally or even more than that actual sin, which was a singular act.
651: If therefore Adam's actual sin is imputed to us, his vice—or habitual and implanted sin—is imputed to us too. If it is imputed, it is not in us. For what Adam shared with us by imputation he did not share with us by real existence. The sin we sinned in Adam's person we did not really sin in our own persons after we were born.
652: Otherwise we would be born from Adam more sinners than Adam was. For to him was imputed only his own actual and habitual sin; to us both would be imputed as to Adam, and besides there would be imputed a habitual sin of the same kind actually implanted and inherent in us—for, like it or not, innate corruption is sin, and unless forgiven is to be imputed unto death.
